description:
`me` lets an app you authorize read selected profile facts, intents and matching preferences, and update them only if you allow it.

The gateway answers `me` itself (`me://user`), with no seller upstream or billing. Reads project only the calling key's explicit `service:me` read grant from the account routing context; absent and unshared values are indistinguishable. Each resource has a separate grant option: `profile` selects existing dotted profile paths, while `intents` and `preferences` select flat categories of natural-language items. Missing options grant nothing. A granted category includes its private and public items and future additions. Write grants permit profile-section merging or whole-category replacement, subject to account edit authority; service writes cannot publish new or changed public content. One permission set applies to all resource selections in the grant. `me` exports read and write, with no invoke; broad `service:*` or `*` alone never grants data access. A sole `*` selector covers all current and future categories only on a manually created, unbound key; enrollment-bound/delegated keys must name categories.

GET /me remains the profile alias; GET /me/intents and GET /me/preferences read the corresponding granted categories, and a single category is reached at /me/intents/travel or /me/preferences/reading. For example, a service:me grant with permissions ["read","write"] and options "intents=travel&preferences=reading" permits both operations on both categories. POST /me/intents/travel with {"data":[{"text":"Visit Japan next spring.","public":false}]} replaces that list and acknowledges only {"name":"travel"}. Existing profile writes remain POST /me with {"name":"<section>","data":{...}}, without a publication flag. See How to use this service for grants, item limits, attachment references, and deployment prerequisites.

intents.description: Desired upcoming actions, such as travel or needs. List up to 64 distinct flat categories (lowercase letter first, then lowercase letters, digits, _ or -, at most 64 characters). Read includes every public/private item and later additions within these categories. Write replaces each whole category, including owner/other-app items, but cannot publish new/changed public items. Unset grants nothing. A sole * covers all current/future categories only for a manually created unbound key; never mix * with names or use it for an enrollment-bound/delegated key. The grant permissions apply to every selected resource.

preferences.description: Matching tastes and constraints, such as reading or tools. List up to 64 distinct flat categories (lowercase letter first, then lowercase letters, digits, _ or -, at most 64 characters). Read includes every public/private item and later additions within these categories. Write replaces each whole category, including owner/other-app items, but cannot publish new/changed public items. Unset grants nothing. A sole * covers all current/future categories only for a manually created unbound key; never mix * with names or use it for an enrollment-bound/delegated key. The grant permissions apply to every selected resource.

profile.description: Profile paths this grant covers (the profile resource's option; each me resource has one named after it): a section name (research), or a section followed by keys of its object data (address.state). A read returns these paths where they are set. A write needs the whole section listed. * is the whole profile, for keys you create yourself only. Unset covers nothing.

name: me

payout_price.description: Not billed: reading and updating your own profile, intents and matching preferences is free

summary: Share selected profile facts, intents and matching preferences through /me; authorize reads and writes independently.
